newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss watchmaker dismisses Swatch takeover talk.
newsitem.headline: Swiss watchmaker dismisses Swatch takeover talk.

text.p: Swiss luxury and jewelled watchmaker Patek Philippe, whose clients have included Albert Einstein, Rudyard Kipling and Walt Disney, dismissed reports on Thursday that modern watchmaker Swatch wanted to take it over.

Patek Philippe president Philippe Stern said Nicolas Hayek, president of Societe Suisse Microelectronique et d'Horlogerie SA (SMH), who launched the popular Swatch brand, had contacted him expressing interest in buying a large stake in his company.
But Stern denied plans to sell the family-held Geneva firm fully or partially.

"We are not for sale," Stern told Reuters. Asked what triggered Swatch's interest, he said: "I don't know. It was maybe in his (Hayek's) dreams. Perhaps it was jealousy because we're very successful. We will remain independent."

The daily Journal de Geneve reported that Hayek wanted to acquire Patek Philippe fully or up to 49 percent of it. Hayek later said in a statement that he had had contacts with Stern, but that Patek Philippe was not for sale.

The Swiss watchmaking industry has seen a series of takeovers amid rising competition. Patek Philippe, Audemars Piguet, Girard Perregaux and Rolex remain virtually the only completely independent luxury watchmakers.

Vacheron Constantin, the world's oldest top-quality watchmaker which was owned by former Saudi Oil Minister Sheikh Ahmed Zaki Yamani, was sold in December to Vendome Luxury Group, whose brands include Cartier, Piaget and Dunhill.
Other acquisitions were of Jaeger LeCoultre, Breguet and Baume & Mercier -- the latter also by Vendome.
Patek Philippe's make of luxury wristwatches, which can have up to five-figure price tags, are avidly sought by the rich.
Its 625 employees produce about 20,000 watches a year with a waiting list for some of its more complicated pieces.
Turnover was 250 million Swiss francs ($170 million) in 1996. It has embarked on a 200 million Swiss franc ($136 million) investment programme to construct a new factory.
Swatch, developed by Hayek, is a brand of fun wristwatches which was initially meant to be a cheap, disposable watch until the company began producing special and limited collections.
The more sought-after pieces like the jelly-fish, the hocus-pocus and Hollywood Dream can cost thousands of dollars.
